sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Whole entry point
sections.what: Runs the solar import as one flow: protects the original results, reads the approval for a commit, runs the import, saves the output files, and prints a summary of the results and any held rows.
sections.why: Reason for the single flow is not stated in the code. The protection of original results is explained in the code message.
sections.watch_out: Commit trusts the saved dry-run file for approval, so that file must be the one that was reviewed.

summary: The entry point for the solar report import. It runs a dry run or a commit, saves the results to files, and refuses to import again once the original commit exists unless rerun is requested.
purpose: Run the solar import safely and keep a record of each run.
why: The code keeps the original before and commit reports unchanged, stated in the message when a repeat is refused.
how: Creates the output folder. If committed.json already exists and rerun is not set, it stops. In commit mode it reads the earlier dry-run file and passes its digest for approval. Calls the solar import, writes the result file, prints a summary with the held rows, and exits with success or failure.
inputs: The dry-run.json file from an earlier run, needed for commit. The --commit and --rerun flags. The solar import module and manifest.
outputs: dry-run.json or rerun-plan.json, committed.json or rerun-commit.json, and a console summary.
risks: Commit reads its approval from a saved file, so an old file could approve a different plan. The digest check happens inside the solar import module, which is not shown here.
debug: If the run stops with a message about immutable reports, check whether committed.json exists and whether --rerun is needed. The held rows list shows the blocker for each held project.
